title: Backpressure: The Reliability Pattern
subtitle: Explicit pushback caps work-in-progress to keep latency bounded and outages contained.

panels.heading: The comforting trap
panels.caption: We queue and retry to be 'reliable', hiding overload until latency collapses.
panels.note: Unbounded work in progress turns bursts into long delays and cascading failure.

panels.heading: What really happens
panels.caption: Open-loop retries amplify load; autoscaling reacts late; queues grow; SLOs are blown.
panels.note: Without feedback, clients push harder exactly when servers are slowest.

panels.heading: Deliberate pushback
panels.caption: Cap in-flight work, send clear 429/503 or hints, and respect backoff with retry budgets.
panels.note: Bounded WIP with explicit signals turns overload into a stable plateau.

strip_title: How to design and verify pushback
strip_caption: Practical moves to add backpressure, avoid hidden queues, and keep clients civil.

steps.label: Set hard WIP bounds
steps.detail: Gate in-flight ops; prefer fast failure.

steps.label: Return clear pushback
steps.detail: Use 429/503 or error hints to slow senders.

steps.label: Protect fairness
steps.detail: Per-tenant caps; borrow idle with care.

steps.label: Prove it under stress
steps.detail: Burst test; watch queue depth and p99.
